outline.chapter_title: Chapter 1: Beyond Tokenization – The Case for Raw Byte Processing
outline.description: Introduces the fundamental problem of tokenization in Large Language Models (LLMs), discussing its inherent biases, inefficiencies, and inability to generalize across modalities. Sets the stage for the need for a novel architecture that can process raw bytes efficiently at scale.
subtopics: The Heuristic Nature of Static Tokenization: Limitations in Multilinguality and Noise Robustness
Why Previous Byte-Level Approaches Failed at Scale: The Cost of Sequence Length
Computational Bottlenecks in Transformers: Why Feed-Forward Layers Dominate Byte Costs
The Core Insight: Dynamic Computation Allocation Based on Information Density

outline.chapter_title: Chapter 2: The Anatomy of Patching Strategies
outline.description: Provides a technical breakdown of how raw bytes can be aggregated into computationally manageable 'patches.' Compares static versus dynamic segmentation methods and introduces the concept of entropy-guided partitioning.
subtopics: Static Segmentation: Fixed-Stride and Whitespace-Based Patching
Dynamic Segmentaton Principles: Defining the Ideal Information Boundary
Deriving Entropy Estimates from Lightweight Auxiliary Language Models
Algorithmic Implementation: Global Thresholds vs. Approximate Monotonic Constraints
Incremental Patching Requirements vs. Traditional BPE Non-Incrementalism

outline.chapter_title: Chapter 3: Architectural Design of the Byte Latent Transformer (BLT)
outline.description: Deep dives into the structural components of BLT, detailing the interaction between the lightweight local models and the powerful global transformer. Explains how information flows through encoding, mixing, and decoding stages.
subtopics: High-Level Overview: Separating Local Detail from Global Reasoning
The Latent Global Transformer: Managing Variable-Length Patches Efficiently
- Incorporating Hash N-Gram Embeddings for Rich Context
- Implementing Cross-Attention Mechanisms to Pool Bytes into Patches
